own_solution.law: For insertion depth x, the air-filled and dielectric-filled regions act as parallel capacitors: C(x)=C0[1+(kappa-1)x/L]. Including the battery's work, the force at fixed voltage is F=(1/2)V^2 dC/dx=(1/2)V^2 C0(kappa-1)/L. Here dC/dx=6.00e-9 F/m, giving F=7.50e-4 N.
assumptions: The dielectric obeys the stated linear model with relative permittivity 4.
The slab fills the plate separation and width over the inserted length.
The slab's advancing edge remains within the plates and away from their ends.
The ideal battery maintains the applied voltage; fringe fields and friction are neglected as instructed.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T9C5B and T8F88 specify only a 'small battery', whereas their numerical counterparts T09BD and TABCB specify 350 V, violating the required preservation of the quantity's number and unit.

notes: The base physics and all individual added-sentence problems are solvable. The invalid verdict concerns the required numerical matching between variants. For TBFE0 and TE652, the series-aiding batteries impose 850 V, giving 0.0021675 N. The earlier-run batteries have no effect on the present configuration, and the Geiger counter's independent supply has no stated coupling to the capacitor. Insertion depth appears in C(x) but disappears from dC/dx, so TA3FF and TAC6D are classified C within the explicitly stated partial-insertion geometry.
